I have sort of mixed feelings about it.

On the one hand, the whole concept of "illegal art" is sort of asinine, so I tend to like anything that upsets that.

On the other hand though...

Galleries and museums and such are nice places to visit largely because they're filtered. See... the world is stuffed full of people who think they're artists, but who just... well... suck at it. Go somewhere that's unfiltered (deviantArt is a fine example) and just browse around and you'll see. There's an awful lot of really godawful stuff that people do, and the really nice pieces are actually few and far between.

The problem with street art is that there's no filter AND there's no getting away from it. If I go to a gallery, I expect to see quality art. If I go to deviantArt, I can just ignore the crap. But if I'm walking down the street and some lousy, no-talent "illegal street artist" has decided to thrust his "art" on the community, it's there, bigger and bolder than life, and there's no getting away from it.

That, to me, is not only irritating, but rude. I have no interest in looking at crappy art, and I sure as hell don't want it forced on me. If someone's that desperate to express himself, he can do the same thing other people do and get a dA account, and then I can just ignore his crap art.

Now, all that said, I have seen a bare handful of really impressive works of illegal street art, and I do have to say that they're terrific - the combination of quality art and anti-authoritarianism is pretty hard to beat. But I'm not exaggerating when I say I've seen a "bare handful" of really impressive works. Most of them, unfortunately, have been crap, and unwelcome, unnecessarily in-my-face crap at that.
